proof_steps.claim: Use the probability density normalizations to define a∈[0,1].
Factor |p_+-p_-| as |sqrt(p_+)-sqrt(p_-)|(sqrt(p_+)+sqrt(p_-)); Cauchy–Schwarz and ∫p_±=1 yield TV≤(1/2)sqrt((2-2a)(2+2a))=sqrt(1-a²).
Combine the proven B.7 gap with the preceding inequality: δ≤TV≤sqrt(1-a²) implies a≤sqrt(1-δ²), using a≥0.
Apply log(1-t)≤-t for t=δ² to obtain sqrt(1-t)≤exp(-t/2), i.e. Eq.25.
Use the actual mixture factorization Eq.6 to identify barp_b(x₁,…,xₖ,z)=∏p_b(x_j)φ_m(z) when m>0.

Tonelli factors the total affinity into the product of k single-block affinities and the residual integral 1, giving a^k. When m=0 the source instead omits the residual factor and obtains the same a^k.
The probability-density identity TV=1-∫min and min(u,v)≤sqrt(uv) give TV(barπ_+,barπ_-)≥1-a^k.
Raise the nonnegative Eq.25 bound to integer k, then take complements to obtain the final Ex72 inequality.

assumptions.analysis: Cauchy–Schwarz supplies TV(P_+1,P_-1)≤sqrt(1-a²); log(1-t)≤-t applies to t=(1/4)exp(-10n/sqrtκ)∈[0,1). Tonelli applies to the nonnegative product affinity integrand. k is a nonnegative integer, in fact ≥1 here, permitting the kth-power bound.
assumptions.construction: The P_b and barπ_b are the Gaussian mixtures defined by the actual determinant-conditioned construction, not arbitrary measures identified solely by a name.
assumptions.independence: Averaging independent O_j under each D_b produces the product P_b^⊗k. The same residual factor appears on both sides. Independence is conditional on the selected sign, not after randomizing that sign jointly.
assumptions.normalization: p_±1 are nonnegative probability densities, so ∫p_±1=1 and 0≤a≤1. When m>0 the common residual density φ_m is nonnegative and integrates to 1.
assumptions.regularity: Orthogonality gives I_n≼A_O≼κ I_n, hence valid nonsingular Gaussian targets, and the block precision including any residual belongs to A_(d,κ).
assumptions.single_block_input: Proposition B.7 proves TV(P_+1,P_-1)≥(1/2) exp(-5n/sqrtκ), using n≥3 and κ≥4. Ex72 does not independently assume this estimate without its upstream source boundary.

conclusion.kind: Explicit finite-parameter lower bound with the displayed inequality directions. The final exponential estimate is not an equality assertion.
conclusion.target_of_distance: The two averaged target laws, not two algorithm output laws, not their componentwise TV distances, and not individual fixed-precision Gaussian targets.

constants.block_bound: a^k≤exp{-(k/8)exp(-10n/sqrtκ)}; final complement is 1 minus this expression.
constants.exactness: All constants are the explicit source constants; there is no unspecified universal constant or asymptotic/O notation in Ex72.
constants.origin_of_1_over_8: Squaring 1/2 produces 1/4, then the square root/log estimate contributes another 1/2, giving 1/8. The 10 in the exponent is twice the single-block 5.

domains.domain_boundaries: The separation claim is in the n≥3, κ≥4 standing regime of B.2 and the §3.1 construction. n need not be odd. The later choice n=2T+1 is a main-theorem application, not a hypothesis of Ex72.
domains.orthogonal_group: O(n)={O∈R^(n×n):OᵀO=I_n}. The precision class is A_(d,κ)={A=Aᵀ:I_d≼A≼κ I_d}.
domains.parameters: d and n are integer dimensions with 3≤n≤d; κ is real with κ≥4; k=floor(d/n) is the number of blocks; m=d-kn is an integer with 0≤m<n and k≥1.
domains.spaces: The underlying sample spaces are Euclidean spaces with their measurable/Borel structure; x_j∈R^n and, only when m>0, z∈R^m; product coordinates identify the total space with R^d.

objects.affinity: a=∫_(R^n) sqrt(p_+1(x) p_-1(x)) dx is the single-block Hellinger affinity, with 0≤a≤1.
objects.densities: p_O is the Lebesgue density of N(0,A_O⁻¹), p_b the Lebesgue density of P_b, and barp_b the Lebesgue density of barπ_b. For m=d-kn>0, φ_m is the normalized standard Gaussian density on R^m.
objects.haar_and_priors: O(n) has Haar probability; μ_(n,b) is Haar conditioned on det O=b, b∈{-1,+1}. Under D_b, O₁,…,Oₖ are independent draws from μ_(n,b), and D_b is the law of A_𝐎. Each of the two determinant components has full-Haar probability 1/2.
objects.targets: π_A=N(0,A⁻¹); P_b=E_(O∼μ_(n,b))[N(0,A_O⁻¹)] on R^n; barπ_b=E_(A∼D_b)[π_A]=P_b^⊗k ⊗ N(0,I_(d-kn)) on R^d, with the final factor omitted when kn=d.

quantifiers.excluded_imports: No query budget T, algorithm, output law, target accuracy ε, indistinguishability assumption, or randomized common-sign mixture is quantified in the Ex72 separation result itself.
quantifiers.main: For every permitted d,n,κ, form k and the two actual priors and averaged targets as above; the resulting pair barπ_+1,barπ_-1 satisfies the final lower bound.
quantifiers.proof_points: The density product is for each b and each product-coordinate point (up to density versions); the min≤sqrt pointwise inequality is for nonnegative density values, and the integrals are over the full relevant Euclidean spaces.
quantifiers.signs: b ranges over exactly {-1,+1}; all k blocks share b, while the O_j are independent within each fixed-b prior.

senses.arithmetic: exp and sqrtκ use real arithmetic; κ≥4 makes sqrtκ positive and all divisions meaningful. k is an integer power/multiplicity, read as its real value in k/8.
senses.hellinger_convention: a is unsquared affinity ∫sqrt(pq), not Hellinger distance or squared affinity. Tensorization yields a^k, with the shared residual contributing a factor 1.
senses.overlap_convention: For normalized densities, TV=1-∫min(p,q). The factor 1/2 in the L1 convention is essential to both this identity and the single-block affinity calculation.
senses.probability_and_averaging: Haar measures and Gaussian laws are probability measures. P_b and barπ_b are mixtures/averages of target laws. The density of a mixture and the product structure are at the distribution level.
senses.residual_convention: If kn<d, retain the identical standard Gaussian residual on R^(d-kn) and its integral 1 in the density/affinity product. If kn=d, omit the final Gaussian/identity block and every residual integral; the source explicitly uses this omitted-factor convention rather than requiring a density on R^0.
senses.tv_convention: TV(P,Q)=sup_(measurable B)|P(B)-Q(B)|=(1/2)∫|p-q|dλ, for probabilities with densities with respect to any common dominating λ. Its range is [0,1]. A measurable [0,1]-valued test h has |E_P h-E_Q h|≤TV(P,Q).

upstream_boundaries.closure: The source includes the spectral verification in B.3; basic Gaussian/probability conventions are standing definitions.
upstream_boundaries.content: Haar probability and its two equal-mass components; centered target π_A=N(0,A⁻¹); the exact A_O/A_𝐎/prior/averaged-target definitions; orthogonality and Cauchy–Schwarz prove the precision spectral bounds. Symmetry plus positive definiteness ensures Gaussian densities. Identity residual is explicitly omitted when m=0.

upstream_boundaries.closure: This is an actual source-proved identity for the real orthogonal construction; it is not an unconstrained symbolic cancellation assumption.
upstream_boundaries.content: For any Borel h with E|h(U)|<∞, U=O_11 under full Haar, E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)h(U)]=((-1)^(n-1)(sqrtκ-1)^(n-1)/2^n) E[((sqrtκ+1)U-(sqrtκ-1))h(U)]. Factor A_O as one quarter BᵀB; B_t=(sqrtκ+1)I-tO stays invertible for 0≤t≤sqrtκ-1 by norm lower bound ≥2||v||, so det B_t is positive. Thus the positive square root of det A_O equals 2^-n det B. Multiply by det O and expand principal minors. Row reflections preserving O_11 cancel all minors containing i≥2, leaving only the empty minor and {1}. |det O_(S,S)|≤1 ensures integrability.

upstream_boundaries.closure: The Poisson representation formula is the external mathematical boundary, cited by the paper as [5, Theorem 1.21]; the cited reference itself was not read. The local lemma wording contains both n≥2 and a trailing n≥3 phrase; the Ex72 dependency uses n≥3, satisfying both.
upstream_boundaries.content: For U the first coordinate of a uniform point on S^(n-1) and 0<r<1: E[(1+r²-2rU)^(-n/2)]=1/(1-r²), and E[U(1+r²-2rU)^(-n/2)]=r/(1-r²). The source derives them by applying the unit-ball Poisson representation to harmonic functions 1 and x↦x₁ at re₁, with normalized spherical measure.

upstream_boundaries.boundary: Proposition B.7 bounded radial test and signed integral
upstream_boundaries.closure: These operations are source-provided analytic steps; an implementation proving only a numeric exponential inequality would leave this actual source input unaccounted for.
upstream_boundaries.content: h_λ(x)=exp(-λ||x||²), λ≥0; H(λ)=E_full-Haar[det(O)∫h_λ p_O]. Equal component masses give H=(1/2)(E_P+ h_λ-E_P- h_λ), and [0,1]-test convention gives TV≥2|H|. Conjugation invariance makes E[det(O)p_O(x)] radial. At ||x||e₁ its exponent depends only on U since e₁ᵀA_Oe₁=(κ+1-(κ-1)U)/2. The source supplies integrable domination (κ/(2π))^(n/2)exp(-||x||²/2), invokes Fubini and Gaussian integration, then B.6 with denominator ≥2+4λ, giving Eq.21.

upstream_boundaries.boundary: Proposition B.7 parameter selection and exact gap
upstream_boundaries.closure: The actual nonzero radial test and its positivity conditions belong to the dependency of the coarse gap.
upstream_boundaries.content: Set q=(sqrtκ-1)/(sqrtκ+1), r=(1-1/n)q, λ=(κ-1)(1+r²)/(8r)-(κ+1)/4=(4n sqrtκ+(sqrtκ-1)²)/(8n(n-1)); then 0<r<1 and λ>0. The denominator is (κ-1)/(2r)(1+r²-2rU)=n(sqrtκ+1)²/(2(n-1))(1+r²-2rU). Since Oe₁ is uniform on S^(n-1), A.1 yields H(λ)=((-1)^n/n)q^n(1-1/n)^(n/2)/(1-r²). The λ=0 match is expressly rejected by the source because H(0)=0.

upstream_boundaries.closure: The constants 5, 10, and 1/8 in the amplification trace to these explicit estimates and the affinity conversion, without asymptotic substitutions.
upstream_boundaries.content: Convexity gives (1-1/n)^(n/2)≥1/2; n(1-r²)=4n sqrtκ/(sqrtκ+1)²+q²(2-1/n)≤4n sqrtκ/(sqrtκ+1)²+2. Together with TV≥2|H| this proves the sharp first bound. For κ≥4, log((sqrtκ+1)/(sqrtκ-1))=2∫₀^(1/sqrtκ)dt/(1-t²)≤8/(3sqrtκ)≤3/sqrtκ, so q^n≥exp(-3n/sqrtκ). Also 2+4n sqrtκ/(sqrtκ+1)²≤2+4n/sqrtκ≤2exp(2n/sqrtκ), giving δ=(1/2)exp(-5n/sqrtκ).

upstream_boundaries.closure: The actual-law identification Eq.6 and the coordinate/residual dimensions must be connected to any abstract product-affinity theorem used later.
upstream_boundaries.content: Block-diagonal Gaussian targets factor for fixed 𝐎. Independent determinant-conditioned O_j under fixed b allow the average of that product to factor into P_b^⊗k. The identical standard Gaussian residual has mass 1. Ex71 is the resulting affinity factorization on R^d.
